title: Peaking for optimal performance: Research limitations and future directions
authors: Pyne DB, Mujika I, Reilly T
population: Athletes across sports (critical review of the taper/peaking literature)
findings: Existing research has defined the taper and examined prescription of training volume, load, intensity, duration and type (progressive or step).
Limitations: lack of studies on team, combative, racquet and precision sports; a relatively small number of randomized controlled trials; narrow focus on a single peak versus multiple peaking.
Limited understanding of the physiological, neuromuscular and biomechanical basis of the taper.
Future research should address the influence of prior training on optimal tapers and interactions between the taper and long-haul travel, heat and altitude.
limitations: Narrative critique with no effect sizes; dated and does not cover ultra-endurance or recreational runners.
implications: Present taper prescriptions as defaults with an uncertainty note and allow user override.
Taper interaction with heat, altitude and travel is unresolved: no numeric adjustment is justified, but surface a note when race conditions are hot, high or need travel.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (J Sports Sci Feb 2009). Included as a critique of the evidence base.
